The midmorning haze of Amphoreus cast a low golden light across the streets, catching in the glassy ridges of the surrounding sanctum and draping the marketplace in a soft, diffused gleam. Amphoreus was beautiful in a way that felt curated, like an oil painting left to bake beneath the sun, and Mydei walked as though he belonged in the centre of it.

He had no need to rush, and yet his stride was purposeful, efficient. Mydei moved like someone for whom grace was muscle-deep; cut into the shape of him, from the drape of his deep crimson robes to the muted glint of metal cresting his boots. The market was crowded, with stalls overbrimming with wares, flora trailing from canopies, and merchants hawking in melodic bursts from behind their counters. He ignored them all,  heading toward the eastern portico, a quiet alcove where -

“ - Mydei.”

The voice, sharp and unmistakable, cut through the din like a drawn blade. Mydei turned instinctively, barely registering the blur of blue and white moving against the grain of foot traffic until they nearly collided.

“Could you please - ” Phainon’s voice snapped, breathless, as he tried to sidestep him. “Sorry, I’m in a hurry - ”

Mydei mirrored the movement automatically, catching the heel of his boot on the uneven stonework. They stepped to the same side, then the other, then again, their bodies half-colliding in a ridiculous, graceless little shuffle that made the man’s eye twitch.

“ Haikas ,” Mydei muttered under his breath, scowling. “Just stop moving so I can - ”

But Phainon didn’t stop, and with a low, frustrated exhale, he simply reached forward, hands gripping firm around Mydei’s waist and hoisting him up like he weighed little more than a rolled-up cloak. It wasn’t rough, not quite, but the sheer ease of it made the breath catch in Mydei’s throat. The press of strong fingers under his ribs, the rush of displacement, the sudden intimacy of being manhandled so casually, without effort or apology.

He didn’t even have time to protest. One moment he was trying to talk sense into him, the next, he was being deposited, placed, on the edge of a nearby stall. Phainon had already moved past, his expression unreadable but focused, too caught up in his own forward momentum to register what he’d just done.

“Sorry,” Phainon called back, half-turning with a crooked, rushed smile. “I’ll see you later!”

And with a flutter, he was gone, swallowed up by noise and shadow and light, the ripple of his departure leaving Mydei frozen, utterly still, blinking after him with a faint frown that wasn’t quite confusion.

What the fuck was that.

He glanced down at himself. His feet still hovered slightly off the edge of the stall, body humming with a foreign tension he hadn’t invited. There were no bruises, nor marks, but the imprint of those fingers lingered all the same.

He shouldn’t be flustered - he wasn’t flustered.

And yet, when he slid down to the ground again, it was with a new sharpness to his breath, as if the air in his lungs was suddenly thicker, warmer. His hands curled reflexively at his sides, palms damp. There was a heat in his stomach now, faint but insistent, lingering in the depths of his chest.
